title: When the Provision Turns
premise: Kestrel Thornbury, a desert ranger drowning in debt, is hired by his old rival Sable Vane to guide a salvage crew to the Provision — a wrecked supply ship rumored to hold enough water-rites and coin to buy a city. But the job was sworn off years ago because the last crew who sought the Provision vanished, and Kestrel's own brother was among them. Racing a rival salvage fleet across six tides of saltflat and drowned canyon, Kestrel discovers the wreck holds not treasure but proof of what his brother found: a map of the deep aquifer that could end the water wars. In the end, Kestrel must choose between paying his debt with the fleet's bounty or burning the Provision forever, and he chooses the fire — walking away nameless, free for the first time.
about_author: Dominic Voss is a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping dry lakebeds across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a converted water tower, where he claims the view of the horizon keeps his plots honest.

chapters.title: The Weight of Nothing
chapters.summary: Kestrel tracks a petty thief across the Saltreach flats, catching him at dusk but letting him go when he learns the man stole only water. POV: Kestrel. Beat: establishes his code, his poverty, and the debt that rules him.

chapters.title: A Compass and a Creditor
chapters.summary: Back in the border town of Marrowgate, Kestrel's creditor Doss gives him ten days to pay or forfeit his ranger's license. His father's compass is all he owns of value. POV: Kestrel. Beat: desperation sharpened by pride.

chapters.title: Sable Vane Returns
chapters.summary: Sable Vane, the rival who ruined Kestrel's reputation seven years ago, arrives with a salvage contract and an apology she doesn't mean. The target: the Provision. POV: Kestrel. Beat: old wounds reopened; he refuses.

chapters.title: Ten Days
chapters.summary: Doss seizes Kestrel's gear; the thief from chapter one reappears, offering information about the Provision in exchange for protection. Kestrel realizes refusing Vane means ruin. POV: Kestrel. Beat: pride gives way to necessity.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Job
chapters.summary: Vane reveals why the job was banned: the last expedition, including Kestrel's brother Alden, never returned. She has new coordinates. Kestrel signs on — not for coin, but for answers. POV: Kestrel. Beat: grief disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Kestrel meets the crew: engineer Brammel, diver Osha, navigator twins Pell and Pim, and quartermaster Hesk who clearly reports to someone else. POV: Kestrel. Beat: distrust as the crew departs Marrowgate at first tide.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Crossing the saltflats, Kestrel spots a second convoy on the horizon — the Corvane fleet, faster and better armed. Vane orders silence. POV: Osha. Beat: the race begins; Osha senses Kestrel is hiding something.

chapters.title: The Drowned Canyon
chapters.summary: The route descends into flooded canyons where the old road disappears underwater. Brammel's engine fails; Kestrel's desert knowledge saves them via a hidden causeway. POV: Kestrel. Beat: grudging respect earned.

chapters.title: What Hesk Carries
chapters.summary: Osha catches Hesk sending signal flares toward the Corvane fleet. Confronted, Hesk admits he's paid to report their position — but not by whom. POV: Osha. Beat: paranoia takes root aboard.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: A sandstorm forces both fleets into the same sheltered basin. Kestrel comes face to face with Corvane's captain, Rell Maddox, who knew Alden. Maddox offers Kestrel a place. POV: Kestrel. Beat: temptation framed as brotherhood.

chapters.title: Maddox's Story
chapters.summary: Maddox claims Alden reached the Provision alive and sent back word — which Vane intercepted. Kestrel confronts Vane; she admits receiving a message but says it named a traitor, not a survivor. POV: Kestrel. Beat: trust fractures along every seam.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: On watch, Kestrel reads Alden's intercepted message stolen from Vane's strongbox: 'The Provision turns. Trust no one who counts.' He doesn't understand it yet. POV: Kestrel. Beat: dread planted like a seed.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: The convoy enters the Glass Reach, where heat mirages swallow landmarks. Pell is lost to a sinkhole despite Kestrel's warning. POV: Pell. Beat: first death; guilt lands hard on Kestrel.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Water rations run short. Hesk stirs the crew against Vane, proposing they sell the coordinates to Corvane. Kestrel backs Vane publicly, privately doubting her. POV: Osha. Beat: loyalty tested without evidence.

chapters.title: The Thief's Map
chapters.summary: The thief's information proves true: a smuggler's tunnel bypasses the Reach. Inside are bones wearing expedition gear — Alden's crew, dead for years. POV: Kestrel. Beat: hope curdles into horror.

chapters.title: Alden's Journal
chapters.summary: Among the bones, Kestrel finds half of Alden's journal. It describes the Provision carrying not cargo but a sealed ledger of the deep aquifer — and warns that one of their own sold them out. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the mission becomes personal reckoning.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Corvane overtakes them at the Silt Gate. A running skirmish costs the convoy its lead wagon. Kestrel saves Vane's life; she almost thanks him. POV: Vane. Beat: rivalry softening into something like alliance.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Vane admits she intercepted Alden's message years ago and buried it to protect her own career. Her apology is real this time. Kestrel walks away from her fire. POV: Vane. Beat: betrayal confessed, forgiveness withheld.

chapters.title: Hesk's Price
chapters.summary: Hesk attempts to steal the journal overnight; Kestrel catches him. Under pressure Hesk names his employer: Doss, Kestrel's own creditor, who wants the aquifer ledger. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the debt was always a leash.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: With one tide left, the convoy reaches the Shallows where the Provision went down. The wreck's mast breaks the surface at low tide — visible only now. POV: Osha. Beat: awe and terror as the goal appears.

chapters.title: Into the Green Dark
chapters.summary: Osha and Kestrel dive the flooded hold, finding the crew compartment sealed from the inside. Someone survived down here long enough to barricade. POV: Osha. Beat: claustrophobic dread beneath the water.

chapters.title: The Turning
chapters.summary: They find the ledger chamber — and understand Alden's words: the Provision 'turns' because the wreck sits over a living aquifer vent that floods the hold twice daily. They have minutes. POV: Kestrel. Beat: revelation under literal rising water.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide Begins
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives at the wreck simultaneously. Maddox takes the crew hostage on the hull, demanding the ledger. Vane negotiates; Kestrel hides the journal pages inside his coat. POV: Kestrel. Beat: standoff at the edge of the tide.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Maddox reveals he was Alden's friend and believes the ledger should fund a war to seize the aquifer. Kestrel argues the opposite. The water begins to rise. POV: Maddox. Beat: two philosophies of survival collide.

chapters.title: The Vent Opens
chapters.summary: The aquifer vent erupts early. The wreck groans; divers scatter. In the chaos, Hesk frees himself and goes for the ledger. POV: Osha. Beat: chaos as nature sides with no one.

chapters.title: Brother's Voice
chapters.summary: Trapped in the flooding hold, Kestrel finds the rest of Alden's journal wedged in a bulkhead — final pages written in the dark. Alden chose to seal the chamber rather than let the ledger be taken. POV: Kestrel. Beat: grief transfigured into understanding.

chapters.title: What Alden Chose
chapters.summary: Kestrel surfaces with the journal but leaves the ledger locked in its case. Maddox sees the empty chamber and understands too late. The sixth tide swallows the wreck whole. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the choice made — memory over wealth.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Low Water
chapters.summary: Hesk, having copied the ledger's key cipher, flees to Corvane. Maddox, humbled, lets the crew go — but warns that Doss will send more. POV: Maddox. Beat: enemies part with reluctant respect.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Back
chapters.summary: The convoy limps home across the flats, burying Pell at the sinkhole's edge. Vane formally dissolves the contract, releasing everyone from shares. POV: Vane. Beat: mourning and quiet absolution.

chapters.title: Debt Collector
chapters.summary: In Marrowgate, Doss awaits with enforcers, expecting payment in aquifer secrets. Kestrel offers instead the truth: the Provision is gone, the ledger drowned. Doss calls his bluff. POV: Kestrel. Beat: confrontation with the man who owned him.

chapters.title: The Cipher Burns
chapters.summary: Before Doss's men can search him, Kestrel burns Alden's journal pages — keeping only the last line in memory. Without the cipher, Hesk's copy is worthless. POV: Kestrel. Beat: freedom purchased with fire.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Doss's creditors turn on him over the failed venture; his empire cracks. The town watches Kestrel walk out of the counting house owing nothing. POV: Osha. Beat: the fall of a small tyrant.

chapters.title: License Returned
chapters.summary: The rangers' guild reinstates Kestrel's license, citing his rescue of the crew. He declines the ceremony, asking instead that Alden's name be entered in the rolls. POV: Kestrel. Beat: honor restored, redirected to the dead.

chapters.title: Osha's Offer
chapters.summary: Osha asks Kestrel to join her diving outfit — a future, offered plainly. He doesn't answer yet. POV: Osha. Beat: tenderness after wreckage; hope made concrete.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Vane departs Marrowgate, leaving a letter: the coordinates of Alden's original camp and her own confession filed with the guild. No request for forgiveness. POV: Vane. Beat: amends made without expectation.

chapters.title: The Camp at Ash Hollow
chapters.summary: Kestrel travels alone to Alden's camp and finds the cairn his brother built before descending to the wreck. He adds a stone. POV: Kestrel. Beat: private ritual; the debt of grief finally paid.

chapters.title: The Thief Again
chapters.summary: The water-thief from chapter one resurfaces, now working a legitimate well crew, and returns the small debt he owed Kestrel: a canteen, filled. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the story's economy of debts closes its circle.

chapters.title: Compass True
chapters.summary: Kestrel opens his father's compass for the first time in years and finds an engraving inside: 'North is a choice.' He sets out on no contract at all, simply walking the range. POV: Kestrel. Beat: identity reclaimed from duty and debt alike.

chapters.title: When the Provision Turns
chapters.summary: Months later, Kestrel guides a guild patrol past the Shallows. At high tide, far off, the sea above the wreck turns slowly green with the vent's light — a grave, a secret, a choice still holding. He rides on. POV: Kestrel. Beat: closure; the price of survival acknowledged and accepted.

chapters.title: North Is a Choice
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Kestrel joins Osha's outfit on his own terms, taking work that pays little and owes less. On the horizon, dust rises — another traveler, another story. He tips his hat and heads north. POV: Kestrel. Beat: resolution — survival without corruption, identity freely chosen.
